en: The Goddess said:
"By your grace, I have understood how to deceive Time."
Now, speak of the medicinal herb that has arisen from the very essence of the mantra.
O Destroyer of Tripura, tell me that ritual procedure which brings about the perfection of existing bodies for their benefit, and which removes old age and disease.
There are many medicinal herbs for the benefit of human beings;
however, first tell me directly that which was previously mentioned by you.
The illustrious Lord said:

"The physician should perform the selection [of medicinal plants] according to the lunar day, asterism, and weekday, as well as the distinctions of the seasons; he should carry out the digging up and extraction with the recitation of mantras."
One who takes medicine at the proper time attains supreme strength; O Goddess, the collection of bark and roots should take place during the autumn and early winter.
In the cool season, one should properly gather fruits along with roots and pith;
in spring, flowers and leaves; and in summer, fruits and seeds.

Even trees that are strong at their own time always lose half their strength when their roots have dried during the rainy season; likewise, it is the same with medicinal herbs regarding their roots and other parts.
This [abundance] occurs in summer and the rainy season; in autumn, it becomes fully complete.
Likewise, the fruit and seed of trees and other plants appear in their own respective seasons.
All medicinal herbs are proclaimed to be powerful on every side,
as are those born in water and on land, as well as trees and creepers.
Village plants, wild shrubs, creepers, and medicinal herbs have been fully described.
A medicinal herb brings about the destruction of disease through its genus, substance, quality, and characteristics.
Likewise, fruits, flowers, and creepers are strong in their own season;
those born in water possess potency at night, while those born on land are strong by day.
Now, the results of the lunar mansions regarding the onset of illness:
Sometimes an ailment arises under Kṛttikā;
in some cases, suffering lasts for nine nights, and under Rohiṇī, it lasts for three nights.
In Mṛgaśīrṣa, death occurs after five nights; in Ārdrā, one is released from life;
and in Punarvasu and Puṣyā, it is ordained that one lives for seven nights.
Likewise, [the rite lasts] nine nights under Āśleṣā; it ends at the cremation ground under Maghā;
for two months under Pūrvaphalgunī; and for fifteen days under Uttarāphalgunī.
In Hastā there is liberation in seven days; in Citrā, for half a month;
in Svātī, it shall be two months; and in Viśākhā, twenty days.
In Maitra (Anurādhā) it lasts for ten days; in Jyeṣṭhā for half a month;
by means of Mūla it is born [in that state]; and the remainder is in Pūrvāṣāḍhā for fifteen days.
For nineteen days it remains in Uttarāṣāḍhā, likewise for two months in Śravaṇā;
for half a month in Dhaniṣṭhā, and for ten days in Śatabhiṣaj (Vāruṇa).
O Goddess, for nineteen days one stays in Pūrvabhādrapadā;
indeed, for three quarters of a day in Vadhra (Pūrvaphalgunī), and for ten nights in Revatī.
One should know that life has reached its end during the day or night under the asterisms Aśvinī and Bharaṇī;
thus one should understand the sequence according to the asterisms as they have been described.
The asterisms Āśleṣā, Śatabhiṣaj, Ārdrā, Svātī, Mūla, and the three Pūrvas; the days of Saturday, Sunday, and Tuesday; and the cruel lunar mansions are unfavorable.
Furthermore, if it is the fourth, eighth, fourteenth, or sixth lunar day, [it is likewise unfavorable].
Avoid this lunar day; it is a time of death for the sick.
On the fifth lunar day falling on a Monday, the second on a Thursday,
and the fourth on a Friday, one should predict death for those who are ill.
For seven days, by means of the conjunction of planets, it is tripled when joined with the lunar day (tithi).
He lives for three months on the food of the lunar day and the lunar mansion.
Now, regarding the signs of death.
The Illustrious Goddess said:
"Indeed, those signs which appear before men's deaths [are as follows]."
O Lord of the World, tell me some of those signs.
The illustrious Lord said:
I shall describe the signs of time that arise for an embodied being when death has drawn near; listen to them in this regard.
If the breath flows through one's nostrils continuously day and night,
his lifespan will indeed be exhausted in three days.
The life-force flows continuously for two days and nights, and then for three days and nights;
thus, his lifespan is said to be exactly one and a half months.
If the wind flows continuously for ten days through both external nostrils simultaneously,
that person lives for two more days.
If one's breath flows from the mouth, bypassing both nostrils,
and remains there for two days, then he shall depart for the city of Yama.
When the Sun is situated in the seventh house and the Moon is situated in the natal ascendant,
that time should be regarded as full, provided the Sun is moving southward.
If one suddenly beholds a man who is blackish-brown,
his own form shall remain alive for exactly two years at that very moment.
If one's semen, feces, urine, blood,
or semen should ever appear here [in the dream] even once, his lifespan is said to be one year.
One who perceives the sky as resembling a sapphire or as smoky over a mountain,
spreading here and there, lives for six months.
One whose death is imminent does not behold Arundhatī, Dhruva, the three steps of Viṣṇu, nor the fourth, the circle of Vāyu.
If one observes the Sun’s daily strength and other factors on the day of Bhādrapada,
or observes them during the [specific] prakṛtis, one will meet with death within six months.
He who perceives colors such as blue and so forth, or tastes such as bitter and sour,
suddenly changing otherwise within six months, is destined for death.
For six months, the throat, lips, tongue, and palate of those in the world of death constantly dry up; they become pale and lose their vitality, with their senses failing one after another.
Semen, armor, eyes, and the ends [of garments] indeed partake of impurity;
therefore, in the sixth month, a man should go to the Kīnāśa-sāgara.
The man who sleeps during the middle of the day while sexual union is underway will certainly become the guest of the King of Dharma (Yama) in the fifth month.
If one's head quickly crosses over the fierce Śakaṭa [asterism] of Mārutyā,
his life will certainly reach its end within six months.
If even one who has bathed well finds his heart quickly parched,
as do his feet and hands, his life remains for only three months.
If one's reflection appears as a fragmented footstep in either dust or mud, that person lives for only five months.
If one's body trembles while the apertures of the body remain motionless,
the messengers of Death bind that man in the fourth month.
He who does not perceive the movement of his own reflection in still water and the like will perish within a month.
Whether on a mountain peak or even on level ground, he does not see the lordly bow;
nor does he see two moons or two suns in the sky during the day.
By day he saw the circle of stars, and by night the sun in the sky;
and simultaneously in the four directions, the arc of Indra’s bow.
On a mountain or on a mountain peak, or in a city of the Gandharvas;
day and night, and dancing—these are the causes of the fivefold state [death].
One whose hearing is obstructed by a prison cell hears no sound;
then, being stout, one becomes thin, and being thin, one becomes stout, until one finally departs from that place.
He who sees his own shadow resting upon the right nostril shall live for five days and then meet his death.
His body is devoured and eaten by piśācas, asuras, crows,
bhūtas, pretas, vultures, jackals, deer, and boars.
Having seen oneself revived in a dream by śarabhas, locusts, hawks, horses, or wolves, one beholds Yama at the end of the year.
A man who sees himself at the time of sleep adorned independently with red garlands of *gaṇḍapuṣpa* flowers and red garments does not live for eight months.
He who climbs a heap of dust, an anthill,
or even a sacrificial post in a dream, perishes within eight months.
He who, during the time of sleep, sees himself mounted on a buffalo, anointed with oil, and adorned with ornaments, goes to the realm of Yama.
He who, within the scope of a dream, sees himself in his own womb or even in his own body,
remains for six months upon blades of grass and dry wood.
He who himself sees a black man wearing black garments and holding an iron staff with a knotted cord shall not survive beyond three months.
He who, even in a dream, should worship Kālīkumārī with the nooses of his arms,
shall not behold the city that is the refuge of Yama for a full month.
A man who, mounted upon a monkey, travels while sleeping toward the eastern direction,
shall behold the city of Śamanātraya within days or months.
He who, by means of the fifth [night-watch], beholds the city of Saṃyamanī, goes to that city of Yama during the fifth night.
Whether a miser becomes generous or a generous person becomes miserly,
and whether their natural disposition undergoes change— when that occurs, they have reached their end.
He who does not see the path of the gods, Dhruva, Śakra, Soma, Chāyā, and Arundhatī— even if he stands far away— shall not live beyond a year.
If one sees the smiling orb of the sun, or fire garlanded with flames,
after eleven months have passed, he shall not live beyond that.
If one is struck by rows of crows on the left while a shower of dust falls,
or if one sees one's own shadow appearing otherwise than normal, one will live for four or five days.
Having seen an unwholesome lightning flash occurring in the southern direction,
or likewise a rainbow of Indra, one's life remains for only three months.
He who sees his own body without a head in oil, in a mirror, or in water,
shall not live beyond a month.
If there is the odor of a corpse in one's mouth, body, and even clothing,
the life of that yogin should be known to last for only half a month.
If the cheek of one who has just bathed dries up quickly,
and he sees water [reflected] in his own husband, his life remains for ten days.
If one sees oneself traveling toward the southern direction while mounted on a bear or a monkey in a dream, death will surely come; of this there is no doubt.
If a woman wearing red and black garments sings or laughs and leads one toward the southern direction in a dream, that man does not live.
If one sees in a dream a powerful naked mendicant entering [one's house],
or if one sees him alone belching, one should know that death has arrived.
If a man sees in a dream his own foot submerged up to the head in an ocean of mud, that person dies immediately.
If one sees hair, charcoal, a funeral pyre, ashes, serpents, or a river without water in a dream, death will occur within ten days or on the eleventh day.
If a jackal howls at sunrise while facing someone,
whether in a contrary or favorable direction, that person goes to immediate death.
If, immediately after eating, one's heart is oppressed by hunger and a tingling sensation arises in the teeth, there is no doubt that his life has come to an end.
Seeing Indra’s weapon at midnight, as well as an eclipse of the moon,
one who knows himself should consider his own life to be nearly exhausted.
He whose nose becomes crooked, whose ears undergo depression or elevation,
and who remembers tears in his eyes, shall go to the abode of Yama.
When the face and the tongue constantly take on a reddish hue and appear as if smeared with meat,
then the wise man should recognize that death is approaching him.
One whose ears are blocked does not hear the internal sound arising from oneself;
he in whom the light of the eyes perishes also does not live.
Having understood these signs of time and the many junctions, a person should either practice yoga or go to Kāśī.
I speak this truth regarding the means of deceiving Time:
it exists even without the worship of the Lord of Kāśī, who conquers death.
In the same way, disease is quickly destroyed even without the consumption of medicine.
Now, regarding the uprooting of the medicinal herb:
it should be done on a lunar day that is not cruel (i.e., not the new moon), which is full of victory (the full moon) and free from portents of misfortune.
Soft, light, and dry—these are auspicious for the uprooting of medicinal herbs.
(p. 8) Now, the classification of seasons:
henceforth, I shall fully explain the medicinal application according to the divisions of the seasons.
Likewise, one should apply the day and night, as well as spring and the other seasons, in their proper sequence.
Spring is said to be in the forenoon, summer at midday, and the rainy season in the afternoon;
the following day is seen at dusk.
O Goddess, one should understand the divisions of the seasons according to the sequence of ten *daṇḍas*: Hemanta occurs at midnight, and Śiśira during the remainder of the night.
One should perform rites for subjugation and the like during the spring;
one should practice incantations for causing enmity in the summer, and likewise for driving away enemies during the rainy season.
In the autumn one should perform pacification, and likewise nourishment in the winter;
in the cool season one should perform killing, according to the distinctions of the seasons.
All these seasons have indeed been described in their proper order;
through them, the accomplishment of rites such as subjugation and others occurs with effort in every respect.
One should perform the recitation (*japa*) according to the sequence, mounting it upon the index finger and the other fingers. Now follows the *Citrakalpa*:
red lead (*raktacitra*), lac (*pala*), *viḍaṅga*, and molasses (*guḍaka*).
One should make these equal and, having ground them, proceed to form them into pills.
One should rub it with the juice of *bhṛṅgarāja* for three days;
thereafter, one should consume one [pill] each day.
Elā, Karaka, Kalā, and likewise Nāgeśvara:
[the first] destroys disease within one month, and the fourth bestows the state of Śrī.
In the same way, O Goddess, it destroys goiters and scrotal enlargement;
bestowing strength and nourishment, within six months one becomes like an elephant.
In two months there is an increase in luster, and in three months it destroys leprosy;
in seven months, one will become a learned man equal to Bṛhaspati.
By eating [it] for one year, a yogin shall become equal to me.
(p. 9) Now follows the ritual procedure (*kalpa*) for *maṇḍūkaparṇī*.
Having washed maṇḍūkaparṇī, coptāṭya, and [other herbs] along with their roots on a Sunday coinciding with the Puṣya asterism,
one should then reduce them to a fine powder.
Then, having placed it in a vessel of ghee until the day of Puṣya and the Sun (Sunday),
whoever drinks it along with sour gruel (kāñjika) in quantities equal to a cat’s paw-print [will achieve the desired result].
Having been soaked with milk for one month, it destroys diseases of the teeth;
by consuming it for two months, O Goddess, one likewise eliminates gray hair.
Now, the ritual procedure for *punarnavā*:
On a Monday during the *puṣya* asterism, one should take white *punarnavā* together with its roots and leaves in the morning and have it ground into a fine powder.
Having then kneaded it with ghee and honey,
one should carefully place it in a vessel so that it may serve as a protection.
Then, O Goddess, at the end of that month, during the spring season, one should become pure and composed before the Campaka flower, which has the brilliance of gold.

At that time, her body would become fair-complexioned, with hair resembling the wings of bees, and she would emit a foul odor like excrement and urine. Her speech would be the only thing that remained true.
One who is as eloquent as Bṛhaspati shall live for five hundred years;
there is nothing equal to it, even in an eon—thus has Punarnavā been described.
Through its service, the vital wind (vāyu) becomes stable in the body for an excellent kalpa.
Īśvara said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the excellent kalpa of Nirguṇḍī.
O Goddess, you are the bestower of wealth and grain, and the increaser of longevity and health.
She who eternally bestows peace and nourishment, the Goddess who is the witness and the very embodiment of one's own nature,
is celebrated as Nirguṇḍī, the bestower of happiness upon all the worlds.
Therefore, I shall explain the application; listen, O beautiful one.
(p. 10) The Ritual Manual of Nirguṇḍī.
Having uprooted the root of the nirguṇḍī plant on an auspicious day, and not otherwise.
Having mixed eighteen palas of powder with twelve palas of ghee and sixteen palas of honey according to the prescribed method, [one should consume it].
One should place these for one full month inside a smooth vessel, completely submerged in a heap of grain; after a month has passed, one should remove them.
Having duly honored the Guru as a deity, one should perform worship according to the prescribed rules;
likewise, one should feed Brahmāṇī and Kumārī in accordance with the ritual injunctions.
Having received their instruction and having become pure on an auspicious day,
one should consume the *viḍālapada* [mud] according to the prescribed rite.
The characteristic sign is that one must eat day after day;
furthermore, the limbs, the eyes, and one's own body become strengthened by this very [practice].
One should avoid [these]; thus, free from wrinkles and grey hair, one will certainly become long-lived.
One's semen becomes inexhaustible, and one is capable of approaching a hundred women.
By eating as much as he desires, he is no longer afflicted by those torments;
he partakes of food, sexual union, and sleep according to his own will.
A man is seen to recover properly from mental disorders if he drinks one *prastha* of *nirguṇḍī* powder mixed with an equal amount of cow’s urine.
O Goddess, by practicing this for ten nights, one shall always destroy even the most severe leprosy, just as the wind destroys clouds in the sky.
Whoever drinks the powder of white nirguṇḍī with goat’s urine,
their nails, hair, and likewise teeth will indeed fall out within seven days.
By practicing for two weeks, the accomplishment of yoga will certainly occur;
by practicing for three weeks, these signs arise.
O Goddess, he is not burned in fire, nor does he die in water;
by means of his body, he perceives neither iron nor gold.
By practicing this yoga for four weeks, one may leave the earth and ascend to the sky;
taking the powder of nirguṇḍī, one should consume it with ghee.
Whether one is emaciated or weak, one will certainly regain strength and vigor by taking the powder of nirguṇḍī and drinking it with warm water.
Through practice for seven nights, one is sung of together with the Kinnaras;
having extracted the root of Nirguṇḍī, the wise person should keep it in the house.
All obstacles and all [evil] names perish entirely within the house.
Now, the mantra for consumption:
first the *praṇava* (oṃ), then *māyā* (hrīṃ), the *kūrca* seed-syllable (hūṃ), ending with *phaṭ*.
One should recite the mantra ending with the wife of Vahni (Svāhā) one hundred times over the medicinal herb.
O Goddess, having recited [the mantra], one should consume [it], and the fruit described in the Kalpa shall be attained.
The mantra is: Oṃ hrīṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhā.

O beautiful one, O Goddess of Fire! The wise man, having recited "oṃ hrīṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhā" followed by the two *māyās*, the *kūrca* mantra, and ending with *phaṭ* one hundred and eight times, should consume the medicinal herb.
The mantra: Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ phaṭ svāhā.
Oṃ, salutation to Nāmarūpa, to Pādapā, and to Kubera.
Then, one should consume the medicinal herb with the mantra ending in the wife of Vahni (the fire-god).
One should consume this medicine along with nourishing rice for a moment,
while avoiding alkaline, sour, and similar substances for three nights thereafter.
O Goddess, one should consume the medicine as prescribed and shall obtain the stated fruit;
for as long as one consumes the medicine, one should likewise avoid alkaline substances and the like.
One should avoid salt, oily substances, leafy vegetables, and the like, as well as exposure to wind and sun.
(p. 12) Now follows the ritual procedure for Hastikarṇaka.
In this way, O beautiful one, I shall explain another practice; listen.
A medicinal herb of divine form was previously extracted with the mantra *svāhā*.
He who is known by the name Hastikarṇa is worshipped by the gods;
by merely eating him, one is liberated from all diseases.
Just as deer turn their faces away upon seeing the king of beasts,
even so, upon obtaining this great medicine, every disease perishes.
On an auspicious lunar mansion, under a favorable constellation, on a propitious day, and having performed the excellent worship,
one should face north and offer the arghya with well-guarded, beautiful flowers.
The wise man, having carefully extracted [the essence] with a pleasant mind, should preserve it;
then, having ground it well and prepared it thoroughly, he should cause fine powders to be made.
One should place it, mixed with ghee and honey, in a vessel of clarified butter;
after twenty-one nights have passed, one should extract a portion weighing one pala.
Having fed a Brāhmaṇa, one should then have him recite "Svasti";
thereafter, one should consume [the preparation] mixed with milk day after day.
Merely by consuming a *pala* [of this], one is freed from wrinkles and graying hair;
one becomes a possessor of the Vedas, sweet-spoken, glorious, and like a god.
A man who possesses strength and vigor, being as skillful as Nārāyaṇa,
might travel a hundred yojanas in a single day and return again.
He shall indeed live for a hundred years; there is no need for deliberation on this point.
O lotus-faced one, listen as I describe another application.
If one should consume [the substance] by stirring it into the milk of a black cow, he obtains the previously mentioned fruit; this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt.
Likewise, having stirred it with buffalo milk along with honey and consumed it,
one obtains the three fruits as before within three months.
O Goddess, by consuming [the substance] with curd for three months with diligence,
one obtains the fruit as before; furthermore, the hair shall not turn white.
One attains victory everywhere and the highest power of subjugation;
such a man shall live for two hundred years, equal in strength to a Naga.
Likewise, at the time of going to sleep, by means of water or ghee [applied] even to the size of a cat's footprint,
the perfection of the body will certainly be attained.
Having consumed a hundred palas according to one's desire, one shall become free from old age and death.
This supreme kalpa is to be kept secret, yet it has been revealed to you out of affection.
By the mere service of which a person may attain liberation. Now begins the Śvetārka-kalpa: "Now I shall proclaim the supreme Śvetārka-kalpa."
Listen, O lotus-faced one, to the detailed account of its greatness.
Having carefully uprooted the root of the white Arka plant and reduced it to powder,
one should first pay homage to the Sun and then worship him according to the prescribed rite.
Rising early in the morning at the edge of a dilapidated house, one should drink cow's urine;
thus one becomes wise, a retainer of the Vedas, and free from wrinkles and grey hair.
Equal to Kāmadeva and proficient in all the śāstras,
a man may live for a hundred years through this practice for just one month.
Freed from all diseases and possessing strength equal to that of a Naga,
a man shall travel to another country after binding the root of the white Arka plant to his hand.
Bhūtas, pretas, piśācas and the like, as well as ḍākinīs and guhyakas,
flee upon merely seeing [the practitioner] by the grace of the white arka plant.
One should grind white [orpiment] with yellow pigment and cow’s ghee;
having applied a mark on the forehead, one shall bring the three worlds under one's control.
One should grind white arka together with sandalwood;
by applying this to the private parts, one certainly becomes a kinnarī.
Having bound the root of the white *arka* plant to his hips, a wise man may indeed enjoy a woman;
he shall retain his emitted semen and cause the woman to vomit it.
Having tied white arka and lotus petals around his waist, a man may enjoy a woman;
even if he should enjoy a hundred women, his semen will be retained.
Having brought the root of the white *arka* plant, one should grind it together with one's own semen;
whoever applies this as a tilaka, the entire world shall come under his control.
One's own juice mixed with honey, together with a *tulā* of white *arka*,
will cause semen not to be emitted for as long as the lamp continues to burn.
Having tied the root of that lotus petal at the navel, the Goddess should always hold it in her right hand; thus, supreme good fortune shall arise.
Out of affection for you, the greatness of the Śvetārka-kalpa has been revealed.
It must never be told to a lustful person or to a rogue. Now follows the Bhṛṅgarāja-kalpa.
Now, I shall proclaim the supreme ritual manual (kalpa) of Bhṛṅgarāja:
having diligently ground the roots and leaves of Bhṛṅgarāja into a powder, [one should proceed].

The wise man should grind [the ingredients] with sour gruel (kāñjika) and diligently prepare a pill (vaṭī). He should drink it with care; when taken with one part of water, it will produce its full efficacy.
One should drink an equal quantity of the juice of *bhṛṅgarāja* leaves and black cumin along with oil; by doing so, one becomes free from wrinkles and graying hair.
The juice of *bhṛṅgarāja* combined with the milk of a tawny cow,
when used for just one month, destroys all diseases.
Now, the ritual for *kāchalā*:
O lotus-faced one, listen as I explain the ritual for *kāchalā*.
By binding the root of *kāchalā* on the hand, diarrhea is destroyed.
15) Now, the ritual manual for the *amlālonī*. Now, O fair-faced one, I shall explain the ritual manual for the *amlālonī*.
By administering the juice of amlālōnī, one shall destroy pain in the eyes.
Diarrhea, pain in the navel, and likewise pain in the eyes;
amlālī, sācīmūla, black pepper, and kuṣṭha.
Whoever drinks [this] after having ground it, [the disease] will be destroyed for him during the spring season. Now follows the ritual procedure for *śālmalī*:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the excellent ritual procedure for *śālmalī*.
They are of four kinds: white, yellow, red, and black.
The Brāhmaṇī is white in complexion, and those born of the arms (Kṣatriyas) are yellow;
the Vaiśyas are red, and the Śūdras are proclaimed to be black.
The Goddess consists of the four castes and fashions all beings;
she is white, yellow, and black, yet she is not found everywhere.
I shall not describe that which is red and found everywhere;
having obtained its floral juice, it is prepared through the application of fire.
Having ascertained the strength or weakness of the moon at the auspicious moment,
the wise man, with one-pointed and concentrated mind, should drink two *pala* measures.
Within one watch of the night, intoxication certainly arises;
thus nourished, he lusts after eight women according to his own will.
One should enjoy [the fruits] of one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, and eight [units].
In the first [period], the Goddess is for two palas; in the second, for four.
In the third watch, one should drink exactly six palas of milk, and in the fourth, eight palas; likewise, one should enjoy the sound of singing during each watch.
By this very method, a person shall attain success;
O Goddess, a man shall live for four hundred years, without a doubt.
The man shall possess the strength of a nāga and become equal to Kāmadeva;
he will always be esteemed by women, fortunate, and pleasing to behold.
He becomes swift-moving in nature and is indeed free from wrinkles and grey hair.
The Ritual of Abhayā:
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the excellent ritual of Abhayā;
by consuming it according to the divisions of the seasons, a man becomes equal to a god.
In the autumn it should be taken with sugar; in the winter with ginger;
in the early winter (śiśira) with long pepper; and in the spring with honey.
One who consumes *harītakī* according to this very method— combined with jaggery in the summer and with salt during the rainy season— [attains the desired results].
Through it, one gains growth, strength, vigor, health, and stable youth;
just as fire consumes wood, so does the harītakī consume the impurities of the body.
Sometimes a mother becomes angry, but the myrobalan fruit within her womb never does;
indeed, one who consumes the myrobalan fruit, which brings about well-being, acts just like a mother.
Now, regarding the rule for constellations in the consumption of medicinal herbs: Hereafter, I shall fully explain the constellations that are auspicious for men when consuming medicinal herbs.
Mṛgaśīrṣa, Hastā, Jyeṣṭhā, Mūlā, Viśākhā, Anurādhā,
Dhaniṣṭhā, and Śatabhiṣā are auspicious for the consumption of medicine.
The Goddess said: "Īḍā, Piṅgalā, and Suṣumnā as the third—
this triad of channels is highly praised for the sake of accomplishing the goals of yogins."
O Lord of Gods, by what means are the navel-circles made manifest?
Īśvara said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall explain that which you ask me:
Īḍā, who is cool and has the form of the moon, resides outside the Bherī.
And that [power] is manifested in ghee; therefore, one should drink ghee.
In the right [nostril] is the Piṅgalā channel, possessing a radiance equal to the sun.
That channel of fierce power is illuminated by honey;
and within Mount Meru is the Suṣumnā, whose nature is absolute bliss.
And by the sweet pomegranate juice alone, Suṣumnā is illuminated;
that pomegranate originating from Kashmir is called Miṣṭadāḍima.
Now, the treatment of fever.
Hereafter, I shall fully explain the medical treatment for the occurrence of fever—
whether it be caused by Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, or by a combination of two [humors].
Having cut the root of Keśarāja into seven pieces, one should eat it together with fresh ginger; this destroys even the most severe fever.
One should boil nagara, guḍūcī, dhanyāka, raktacandana, and uśīra— each of these five ingredients combined together— in water.
When only one-fourth remains of that water standing there,
the intense trembling of the Vedas and the fever caused by wind (vātika) are destroyed.
Having tied the root of the Apāmārga plant around the waist with seven red threads on a Sunday,
it quickly destroys tertian fever.
When fumigated with guggulu and the tail [of a cow], one becomes human;
wrapped in black cloth, it destroys quartan fever.
Jambu fruit, turmeric, and the slough of a snake—
this incense removes all fevers and grants sight even to one who is blind.
Now, the mantras for the destruction of fever:
Listen to me as I describe how fever is destroyed by means of mantras.
Oṃ, obeisance to the Blessed One; cut, cut the head of [Name], who is ablaze within the noose of Paśupati! Puruṣāya.
O Goddess of the Gods, with this mantra, "phaṭ," one should perform the cutting of the ground and the limbs.
Then, O Goddess, O Beloved, the great fever comes to an end.
May Devakāṣṭha, Guḍūcī, Dhanyāka, and Raktacandana destroy trembling,
intense pain, and Vātika fever.
Then, O beloved, one should tie the root of *nirguṇḍī* to the hand to remove fever; or else, O dear one, the root of *raktapalāśa* or *apāmārga* may be tied to the hand.
The root of sahadevā, worn on the ear, removes all fevers arising from bhūtas, pretas, and other spirits; likewise, the root of lāṅgalī worn on the neck [achieves the same].
Either the root of *vṛhaspatimūlaka* or the root of *vāḍiyālaka*,
when tied with a thread around the head, destroys even a severe fever.
Having uprooted the root of the *cāpāmārga* plant on a Sunday and tied it with seven threads around the wrist, those [threads] will remove fever from you.
Equal parts of *drava*, ginger, *vāsaka*, and honey,
when consumed for three days, destroy fever that lasts for one day.
Then, O Goddess, if one should obtain dry soil from a ploughshare,
a man should apply that as a *tilaka* upon his bed at dawn.
On a Sunday, one shall destroy a severe quotidian fever.
*Oṃ namo bhagavati chindi chindi the head of so-and-so; blaze up for the Supreme Person, phaṭ!* When a sonless female ascetic died on the bank of the Sarasvatī river, [this was recited].
One should apply a tilaka mark upon that very person, and the fever recurring every day shall be cured.
Thus, with *vīraṇa* leaves, *kañcī* leaves, and *japā* flowers, one performs the libation (*tarpaṇa*) with sesame seeds and water in the "rat-hole" (*mūṣikagarta*).
Now follows the mantra for cutting (*chedanamantra*).
Oṃ! In this most terrible battle of arrows, which possesses a brilliance equal to twelve suns, O Great Hero born of the Eyeless One, release the one-day fever!
One should draw [the diagram] with a horse's hoof and hold the mantra over the vehicle; thus,
a person gradually destroys a fever lasting for a single day by means of the right [hand].
On the northern shore of the ocean dwells a monkey named Dvivida;
he cures a quotidian fever when his image is drawn within the interior of a house.

One should first administer a digestive (pācanaka) formulation consisting of *devadāru*, *dhanyāka*, *nāgara*, and the two types of *vṛhatī*; this removes fever caused by the simultaneous derangement of all three humors (*sānnipāta-jvara*).
O Goddess, at the time of dawn, one should drink a *muṇḍa* [preparation] produced from cow’s urine;
by drinking half that amount, one removes *sannipāta* fever.
The bark and flower of śephālikā, prepared into pills under the asterism Aśvinī and bound with goat hair, remove fever caused by the combination of all three humors (sannipāta-jvara).
Now, the treatment for polyuria:
Hereafter, I shall fully explain the treatment for excessive urination.
One should diligently employ the medicine; otherwise, equilibrium will not be attained.
One should always drink the fresh juice of the *dhātrī* fruit with honey,
O Goddess, or else the alkali of *vāsaka* for the cure of excessive urination and wasting.
Now, the treatment for dysuria (mūtrakṛcchra):
One should cause [the patient] to drink cumin (ajājī), śṛṅgavera, and vīra, along with the whey of curd (dadhimaṇḍa) mixed with salt; this is a remedy that wards off dysuria.
Barley alkali mixed with sugar wards off dysuria;
the wise man who drinks the root of *svarṇaśephālikā* with honey [achieves the same].

It quickly destroys dysuria; this is the truth, the truth—there is no doubt. Guḍūcī with its essence drunk with honey cures urinary disorders. The juice of dhātrī, combined with honey and turmeric, removes all types of meha.
Now, the treatment for the wasting of seminal drops (vindukṣaya):
O Goddess, the man who grinds *ghṛtakumārikā* with milk and drinks it—
even a mere drop— [as well as] *dhātrī* and *bilva* leaves, [is cured].
One should consume *dhātrī* (myrobalan), *harītakī*, and black cumin at the time of retiring to bed; thus, the flow of seminal drops will be brought to an end.
When one has become bound, one should likewise smear the feet with effort;
having taken a ketakī flower, pomegranate, and the root of the vacā plant.

On a Saturday (Bhṛguvāsara), one should consume the milk of a black cow; this will cause the cessation of seminal discharge. By making a pill from the roots of the Bilva and Arka trees under the Aśvinī constellation and consuming it, there is no doubt that this result will follow.
Now, the treatment for *kuraṇḍa*:
O auspicious lady, by grinding *vāha*, *vālī*, and *rājya* together with fresh ginger and applying it as a plaster, one destroys *kuraṇḍa*; of this there is no doubt.
One who is afflicted by that [disease] should prepare a frog using the blood and flesh of a frog;
by applying an ointment of oil made from this to the arm, one brings about the increase or decrease of the swelling.
Having ground blue lotus with clarified butter, it destroys *akuraṇḍa* when applied as an ointment;
or likewise by applying an ointment made from the blood of a house-frog.
Black cumin, ginger, long pepper, and likewise black pepper—this is the essence of the pods; with this, one should combine *karañja* and honey.

Now, the treatment for *kuraṇḍa* (scrotal enlargement) and *galagaṇḍa* (goiter): O Brahman, having ground the root with rice-water, one should apply a plaster for seven days; by this, [there is relief] from *kuraṇḍa* and *galagaṇḍa*.
Now, the treatment for fistula-in-ano (bhagandara):
By applying a plaster of pomegranate root, turmeric, and *ketakī*, the fistula-in-ano shall be destroyed; this is the established method in this formulation.
Now, the treatment for jaundice (kāmalā):
A paste made from equal parts of ghoṣā-phala certainly destroys jaundice.
Alternatively, one should prepare a destroyer [of jaundice] using two parts of guñjā-seeds.
Having expelled the corrupted phlegm, the hand is released from great desire.
21) Now, the treatment for discoloration:
with black sesame seeds together with white mustard, as well as black cumin.
Having ground these in equal proportions, one shall indeed remove discoloration through massage.
Now, the treatment for cough:
Triphalā and trikaṭu, powdered in equal parts and consumed with honey, destroy chronic cough.
One should cook the root and leaves of *bālaka* with ghee;
by consuming this for three days, asthma and cough will be cured.
One should indeed drink an equal amount of the powder of pippalī, devadāru, and śuṇṭhī with warm water; it destroys upward-coursing asthma (ūrdhvaśvāsa).
Now, the treatment for consumptive cough (kṣayakāsa):
One should drink the root of Nāgakeśara together with honey;
or the root of Vāsaka taken with Adhyajala water destroys the disease of consumption.
One should consume the roots of the *aśoka* tree with goat’s milk;
this root, known as *jīveśvarī*, together with honey, brings about the destruction of the disease of consumption (*kṣayaroga*).
Either the root of gavedhuka taken with honey,
or the root of pippalī with milk, destroys the disease of consumption (kṣaya).
Now, the treatment for nasal polyps (*nāsārśas*):
One who thoroughly grinds together *dūrvā*, pomegranate flowers, *āmrātaka*,
and *harītakī* removes the discharge of blood from the nose.
Now, the treatment for hemorrhoids (gudārśas):
One should apply long pepper (pippalī) and turmeric (haridrā) combined with cow’s urine as an insertion into the anal opening to eliminate hemorrhoids.
Haritaki, honey, sugar, and long pepper, when taken together, quickly remove worms from the body; there is no need for further deliberation on this matter.
(p. 22) Now, the treatment for earache (karṇaśūla):
When there is intense pain within the ear, accompanied by sound and an increase in discharge;
Once freed from colic, one should administer it to the stomach, dusted with rock salt.
Having taken an arka leaf, one should warm it slowly over a mild fire;
having crushed it, one should fill the ear with it, and the earache will be destroyed.
One should fill the ear with śatāvarī and taṇḍulīya mixed with honey; it destroys earache. Now I shall tell you an excellent formulation.
Śatāvarī and Taṇḍulīya, used as ear-drops with honey, destroy earache; this I declare to you.
Now, the treatment for eye diseases:
By filling the eyes with the juice of *nimba* leaves combined with *guptī*, eye pains are destroyed; likewise, by using buttermilk, *badara* fruit, and radish.
The blood-bile of a crow and the eyes of a mendicant—
the excellent practitioner, being diligent, should take these and prepare them together in one place.
On an auspicious day, at twilight, one should cause it to be placed between the eyes;
even in darkness, O Goddess of Gods, it produces divine vision.
The wise one should fill the eyes with the resin of the *hastiśuṇḍī* plant;
the disease born of the eyes is certainly destroyed—listen, O Pārvatī!
Now, the treatment for diseases of the head: One should prepare a medicinal decoction by adding viḍaṅga, sulphur, blue lotus (nīlotpala),
cow’s urine, and mustard oil, and then carry out the cooking process.

O Goddess, by drinking the *śivaprāṇa* [the vital breath of Śiva], one shall destroy headache. Having ground black sesame seeds with milk, one should apply the paste upon the head; or else, with the root of *guḍūcī*, the pain of the head goes to destruction.
(p. 23) Now follows the treatment for Padmagandha:
turmeric, salt, black pepper, and white mustard.
Having combined them and ground them together, one should hold them in the mouth and chew them.
Now, the treatment for dental diseases:
One should hold the root of keśarāja together with fresh ginger;
then the teeth will not fall out, provided it is not the root of oḍa.
One should apply heat from an *arka* leaf to the tooth and cause it to sweat;
then the tooth will not fall out due to the chewing of *vakkula* bark.

A powder made from equal parts of cinnamon leaf (*jātīpatra*), hogweed (*punarnavā*), *tila* seeds, long pepper (*kaṇā*), black gram (*kodanna*), costus (*kuṣṭha*), sweet flag (*vacā*), ginger (*śuṇṭhī*), lampblack (*dīpa*), and myrobalan (*harītakī*), when held in the mouth, [removes bad breath].
It subdues wind, pacifies worms, itching, and colic; it destroys all diseases, eliminates foul odors and other defects, pacifies all humors, and the tooth becomes like a diamond.
Now, the treatment for diarrhea.
Now, listen to the application for diarrhea and bloody diarrhea,
by which one is liberated from the disease through the mere use of a small dose.
Having bound the roots of Sahadevā and Kṛtyā, divided into seven pieces,
with red threads around the waist, it destroys all types of diarrhea.
He who drinks tālamūlī with an equal portion of honey [is cured];
for blood-dysentery and consumption, one should drink coconut water.
Now, the treatment for *pariṇāma-śūla*:
Having ground *hiṅgu*, *lavaṅga*, and the bark of *vakula* and boiled them in water, this is declared to be a remedy that increases [the digestive fire] in cases of *pariṇāma-śūla*.
O Goddess, iron powder combined with the powder of triphalā,
when tasted with honey, is the destroyer of the pain known as nāmākhya-śūla.
One should consume equal parts of red lotus, apāmārga, śobhāñjana, vacā, and salt; by this, nāmaśūla (colic) is destroyed.
O Dear One, deer-horn that has been burnt by fire, combined with cow-dung and *jambu* fruit, when drunk,
brings about the destruction of back and hip pains.
Now, the treatment for eczema (*vicarcikā*):
The root and leaves of castor plant (*eraṇḍa*), radish (*mūlaka*), and the juice of *bhṛṅgarāja*—
having mixed these with sour gruel (*kāñjika*), this ointment removes eczema.
Now, the treatment for the disease of leprosy (kuṣṭha).
Having ground the roots of white and black Aparājitā, an ointment is applied for the condition of leprosy. Alternatively, a pill is made from the root of Pāribhadra mixed with meat.
The consumption of these [medicines] cooked with oil destroys leprosy;
likewise, [those] prepared with ghee or even with warm water destroy all forms of leprosy.
Whoever daily consumes the powder of Viśvanimba leaves together with Āmalaka fruits, his leprosy (kuṣṭha) is destroyed.
One should mix the seeds of Somarāja with fresh butter;
when tasted with honey, they indeed remove leprosy.
Having prepared a paste from *kuśa* grass, *harītakī*, *dūrvā*, rice, the latex of the *arka* plant, plantains, *vandanā*, and dried alkaline substances, one should apply it as an ointment.
White leprosy (śvetakuṣṭha) causes consumption; [to cure it, one should take] the root of śāciśāka.
Having ground three parts each of trikaṭu, nimba, guḍūcī, and harītakī, along with one part water, this destroys all types of leprosy.
Now, the treatment for splenic disease (plīhāroga):
Having ground *citraka* and radish and made three pills,
their consumption within the ripe pulp of a plantain fruit destroys the spleen.
Now, the treatment for eruptive boils (visphoṭaka):
Having ground black sesame seeds with sour gruel (kāñjika), one should then cook them. O auspicious lady, applying that as a plaster destroys the pain; thereafter, one should maintain purification.
Having asked for equal parts of *bharica*, red sandalwood (*raktacandana*), and water,
one should first give it to the patient at the start; this destroys boils and ulcers.
Having ground the root of mahānasa and stirred it into water with joy,
glandular swellings (gaṇḍaśotha) are destroyed, and likewise eruptive boils (visphoṭa).
Now, the treatment for arbuda (tumors).
Having ground the root of bhūmikuṣmāṇḍa and stirred it with water, one should cook it;
by applying this as a paste to the *uṣṭapheṇa* (goat's froth) [type of tumor], the arbuda is destroyed.
Now, the treatment for burns:
one should grind together equal parts of sesame oil and barley that has been burnt;
by applying a plaster made from that very mixture, one will quickly find relief from the pain of fire-burns.
Sesame seeds burnt by fire, combined with all ashes,
will cause a wound burnt by fire to vanish simply by being smeared with this.
Now, the treatment for elephantiasis (*ślīpada*):
Having uprooted the root of the *arka* plant on a Sunday, its root should be worn with a red thread; by this, elephantiasis is destroyed.
Through the application of a paste of *valā*, *ativalā*, and *lodhra*, elephantiasis (*ślīpada*) is destroyed;
or one should apply a paste of *daṇḍotpala* root together with *haritāla*.

Having ground together nirguṇḍī, keraṇḍa, suvarṇa, yavāhva, mina, and white mustard seeds with effort, one should apply this as a paste; it is highly auspicious and certainly always destroys elephantiasis (ślīpada) that has been long-standing.
Now follows the method for the suppression of sleep:
having ground equal parts of buffalo horn and *kuṣmāṇḍa* (bottle gourd),
one should apply it to the belly and back of the person for whom there is to be a cessation of sleep.
Having ground together the seeds of *śobhāñjana*, the flower of the blue lotus (*nīlotpala*),
and *nāgeśvara* in equal parts, one casts off sleep by smelling [the mixture].
Having ground ripe *vṛhatī* fruits together with *madhuyaṣṭi*,
one should apply this as an ointment for the eyes to anyone; it will certainly destroy sleep.
Now, the treatment for sleeplessness:
One should place the root of *kākajaṅghā* upon the head,
accompanied by the mantra, for those whose sleep is exceedingly powerful.
The mantra is as follows: Oṃ siddhe siddhe yoginī mahānidre svāhā.
One should worship the goddess Mahānidrāyānī with this mantra.
In that very same way, one should recite the mantra a hundred times within the house;
having become the Great Sleep-inducer, all people will be made to sleep.
One should cast the body into the cremation ground; [the materials are] black earth, cow urine, and clay.
Thus, the illusion consisting of sleep has been described by me in brief.
Now, another method for the mantra of sleep is described,
by the mere recitation of which sleep occurs otherwise.
Now follows the method for invisibility:
the blood and bile of a *daṇḍaka* crane,
and the bones of a jackal, a bear, and a peacock, [taken] from the left and right [sides].
Having ground these together in equal parts, one should then form them into pills;
one should let them dry in the shade and then administer them as an ointment.
O beautiful one, remain as long as it takes for [the gaze] to stay fixed on the eyes so that you become invisible;
likewise, the wise have determined this method regarding the feet and the breasts.
A person who has been fumigated with these— citrāgni, the excrement and foam of a wagtail, and śobhāñjana— is freed from eye diseases.
O beloved, [this is true] even for all the gods who are invisible, let alone for humans.
Now follows the method for seeing the invisible treasure.
One should uproot the root of the *kanakadhustūra* as well as that of the seven-petaled lotus (*saptadala*) while one's hair is loose, and likewise the root of the *avatta* with its bark.
Holding it in his mouth for that long, he perceives everything through men,
reaching down to the depths of Pātāla, wherever a treasure may be located.
Now follows the ritual application for breaking the shackles.
Therein is the sādhana of Kālī. First, the visualization:
[one should visualize her] clothed in red garments, anointed with divine perfumes, three-eyed, and with a smiling countenance.

"O Goddess Kātyāyanī, lift me up— you who have four arms, are adorned with a jewel-crown, ride upon a corpse, are decorated with a garland of severed heads, and hold a curved knife and a skull-bowl. Having thus meditated, one should recite the mantra.
Having uprooted the root of Kṛṣṇajayantī on a Saturday or Tuesday, one should eat it oneself with betel leaf within one's own body.
O Goddess of the gods, the practitioner should utter the *phutkāra* with this mantra;
having recited the mantra one thousand and eight times, he shall achieve success.
The accomplishment of the task will truly come to pass; there is no need for further deliberation on this point.
*Oṃ cāmuṇḍe vajrapāṇi drū-īṃ phaṭ svāhā*.
By reciting this one thousand times, bondage shall certainly be liberated.
O Goddess, the auspicious [mantra] necessarily breaks chains and door-bolts;
it cuts the net of the servant and paralyzes the oil-press.
The potter’s cooking would perish, as would the milk of cows;
now, for removing the foul odor from the body:
sesame seeds combined with mustard, turmeric, and methikā.
Having ground it, by applying it as a thick ointment, the odor of the body is destroyed.
By applying a paste of *ārdraka* flowers together with *tumbī* leaves and *lodhra*,
one removes foul body odor.
(p. 28) Now, the production of fragrance for the body:
take dried mango seeds, *harītakī*, and the pulp of *āmalaka*.
Anointing after eating increases the fragrance of the body.
Having reduced kuṣṭha to powder and consuming it with honey and ghee upon rising in the morning, one acquires the fragrance of a lotus.
Now, the production of luster:
having made a powder of *atasī*, black gram, and wheat, as well as long pepper,
the wise man should smear the body with these together with clarified butter.
From the application of this ointment, one will possess a splendor like that of Kandarpa at all times;
having taken the flowers and the fruit of the dhātrī tree, one should apply it there.
One should grind the sour juice of the rose-apple fruit with honey;
by merely applying this to the genitals, a woman becomes like a beloved and moves [with passion].
Now, the method for generating nourishment:
One should grind dhātakī and somarāja together with milk;
one will become stout and free from weakness—of this there is no doubt.
Now, the method for producing fragrance in the mouth:
One who takes powdered kuṣṭha mixed with kakkola, along with honey and ghee,
for the duration of one month, attains a mouth that resembles the flower of the ketakī.
Now, for the production of a beautiful voice:
one should prepare a powder from these— turmeric, *vacā*, costus, long pepper, *yamānī*, black pepper, rock salt, and ginger.
Having ground the powder together with honey on a stone slab,
if it is consumed continuously for seven days,
men will attain a beautiful voice and sing along with the Kinnaras.
Having rubbed yellow orpiment with the ashes of plantain leaves using a single application, the falling out of body hair occurs.
Now follows the removal of discoloration from the hair:
mustaka, mustard seed, and likewise uśīra;
harītakī, nakha, and āmalakī in equal proportions.
Having removed everything equally and ground it according to the prescribed rite,
one who smears it on the roots of the hair will certainly become equal to a ram.
Now, the application of breast-enhancing qualities:
One should boil oil produced from cultivated sesame seeds with the decoction of *srāvinī* plants;
that oil should then be applied as a *tilaka* mark upon the breast.
Hardness increases and that which had fallen becomes raised;
whether she be old or even a young girl, such is the nature of her breasts.
Having ground the flower of the white *uḍra* plant together with the milk of a black cow, one should apply it to the pair of breasts; thus they will become full.
Combined with *vacā*, *aśvagandhā*, and likewise *aśvārīpatra*,
and joined with the body of *gajapippalī*, it immediately breaks open when applied with water.
Having ground [the ingredients] according to the prescribed method, one should smear it upon the circle of the breasts;
let them fall at any time, just like a raw palm fruit.
One should prepare the decoction by adding an equal amount of *tila* oil and an equal portion of water to the juice of *gāmbhārī* leaves, and then carry out the cooking process.
Having recognized that only oil remains, one should purify the linen with a mantra;
O Goddess, by applying it to the breasts, it certainly becomes like iron.
Now, the production of good fortune:
*keśara*, *nimba*, and the healthy *paṅkaja*.
And the fruit and flower of dhātakī, combined with jambū-milk and uḍhra.
Having ground [the substance] and applied it mixed with honey as an ointment, even a barren woman obtains a son;
one who has recently given birth becomes strengthened, and an unfortunate woman becomes fortunate.
Now, regarding the application to the limbs and the private parts: having fumigated the woman's vulva with neem wood and honey,
that woman shall become fortunate, and her husband will become her servant.
One should grind the flesh of a wagtail together with honey;
by applying it to the vagina at dawn, a man shall become a slave.
By applying buffalo butter, kuṣṭha, and madhuyaṣṭikā to the vulva,
through the power of good fortune, the husband will become a slave.
One should mix buffalo butter with an equal amount of honey,
and having ground the essence of jujube seeds, one should prepare them all together in a single mass.
O Great Goddess, at the conclusion of the crushing [process], a radiant woman shall be produced;
[this occurs when] *gorocanā* has been infused with menstrual blood.
Whosoever beholds this man who has applied that *tilaka*, he shall bring all of them under his control; there is no need for deliberation on this matter.
Rock salt (*saindhava*), black salt (*kṛṣṇalavaṇa*), *sauvīra* salt, and fish gall (*matsyapittaka*),
combined with honey, clarified butter, and sugar— by applying this as an ointment to the vulva,
a man who engages in sexual intercourse will not go to any other woman.
Now, the subjugation of women:
one should gather a flower under Puṣya, likewise a fruit under Bharaṇī,
a sprout under Viśākhā, and a leaf under Hasta.
Likewise, one should bring the root of the *dhustūra* plant for the primary [mantra].
Having ground together gorocanā, saffron, and camphor,
a woman comes under the power of one who applies the resulting mark (tilaka), even if she were Arundhatī herself.
Kokilākṣa, śūkaśimbī, and likewise śatāvarī;
gokṣura, gaṇikāra, and likewise vāṭyālaka.
One should grind the root of the great kuṣmāṇḍa together into a powder and preserve that powder with care in a dry vessel.
O Goddess, one who is composed should drink it with milk at night;
he shall possess manifold qualities and become a captivator of women.
She will become the hand that strikes down the pride of women who have stolen the god of love;
this shall occur under the asterisms of Puṣya, Mūla, or likewise Hastā.
Having brought the root of the white *arka* plant and tied it around her waist, she may engage in sexual union;
she will certainly go to him, even if abandoned by her husband and son, for his sake.

Oṃ cāmuṇḍe, victory! Victory! Paralyze, paralyze! Delude, delude! Subdue all, subdue me and you, svāhā! Having recited this mantra eleven times and consecrated a flower with it, whoever is given that flower shall come under one's control.
Oṃ kāmadeva hastamaparṇa uttama kuru kuru svāhā!
Having empowered [the object] seven times with this, whomever one touches becomes submissive.
I shall now proclaim the mantra in the Apabhraṃśa language for the subjugation of women,
by the mere accomplishment of which there is the supreme accomplishment of power.
The mantra for this is as follows:
O Goddess of Devas, by means of this mantra, she should drink water three times.
Having abandoned everything else, that woman will certainly become his consort.
Now, for generating affection between husband and wife:
one should grind *brahmayaṣṭi*, *vacā*, and *kuṣṭha* together with honey. By anointing her limbs with this, a woman desires no other husband.
O Great Goddess, daughter of the mountain, listen at the time of sexual union:
having taken his own semen, a man should place it in his left hand.
By anointing his left foot with [the paste of] a woman's foot, he becomes dear to women. One should give blue lotus, betel nut, and aparājitā in equal parts.
By the mental longing for whomsoever a beautiful woman comes under control—
[using] *hayamāraka*, madder (*mañjiṣṭhā*), and *mālatī* flowers.
One should grind rice and priyaṅgu together;
by smearing a liṅga with this, a woman will be brought under one's control.
Having ground together the juice of *kapittha*, white lotus, long pepper,
and liquorice with honey, one should apply it as an ointment to the two private parts.
It brings about the affection of a married couple and does not depart even at the end of life;
O Great Goddess, it consists of rock salt, pigeon excrement, and honey.
When the *liṅga* is smeared with these [substances], it brings women under one's control. By constantly smearing the private parts of a husband and wife, it generates love between them.
Furthermore, by means of incense and likewise by applying a forehead mark (*tilaka*), one may bring even a *yakṣa* under subjugation.
Now, the subjugation of the world:
One pala of realgar, along with gorocana and saffron—
by making a tilaka with these, one will undoubtedly bring the world under control.
Sahadeva, Bhṛṅgarāja, white Aparājitā, and Vaca—
by applying a tilaka with these very [substances], one may bring the three worlds under one's control.
Oṃ drū-īṃ! O Gaurī, grant me this good fortune through union.
Having made a powder of realgar combined with *godanta* and the two types of *kākajaṅghā*, he upon whose head it is placed shall become submissive.
Having ground the root of white Aparājitā together with yellow pigment (rocanā),
whoever applies it as a tilaka will undoubtedly bring others under their control.
The mantra for applying the *tilaka* is as follows:
Oṃ raktacāmuṇḍe, bring [the person named] so-and-so under my control, svāhā!
Oṃ drū-īṃ drū-auṃ drūṃ phaṭ—one should recite this mantra ten thousand times.
By means of a forehead mark made with gorocanā mixed with blood, one shall become a subduer.
Having ground the root of *bhṛṅgarāja* and mixed it with semen, one should apply it to the eyes; thus, one shall bring the three worlds under one's control.

Now, the rite of enchantment (*mohana*): Having ground together *bhṛṅgarāja*, the stalk of a blue lotus, and white *gorocanā*, and having applied it as a forehead mark (*tilaka*), one shall enchant the three worlds.
Oṃ sara sara oṃ oṃ svāhā. With this mantra, water consecrated seven times should be applied to the eyes at dawn; it shall delude the three worlds.
Furthermore:
having tied a knot at the edge of the garment with the mantra "Oṃ daṇḍāya mahādaṇḍāya svāhā," one shall delude everyone.

O King, subjects, kinsmen, relatives, brothers-in-law, and friends, cause agitation! Bring them here, bring them here! Enthrall them, enthrall them! Drīṃ drīṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ! May the world come under my control!
Svāhā!
By means of this mantra, one should perform a pleasant cleansing; then everything shall come under control.

Having applied a tilaka on the forehead with the syllable *drū-īṃ* repeated seven times, conjoined with the essence of the flavor of affection (*prītirasamārasa*), whoever knows this shall bring others under their power.
Having uttered his name, one should recite the seed-syllable of Māyā three times;
with hair disheveled and face turned upward, one should perform the cleansing of the face.
"Truly, truly, O Great Goddess, he shall bring everything under his control.
Then follows the production of virility.
Īśvara said:
One should completely avoid food that is excessively salty or alkaline, pungent or bitter vegetables, dried foods, stale food, and eating according to one's own whims.
34) Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the practice that is the cause of virility,
by the mere consumption of which even an old man becomes like a youth.
Having prepared the powder of vidārī and steeped it in its own juice,
one should drink milk mixed with sugar, honey, and ghee after having smeared [the mouth or throat] with it.
O Goddess, an old man shall become young; this is the truth, the truth, and not otherwise.
One should drink the powder of *vidārī* root with ghee and milk.
By nourishing it with the juice of the *auḍumbara* tree, even an old seed becomes young again;
when combined with cow's fresh butter, it will become beloved.
One should quickly kill a cock and likewise [use] the fat of buffaloes;
one should cause it to fall upon those afflicted by worms, and it will be effective—of this there is no doubt.
O Goddess, he who binds the root and the tip of *viṣṇukrāntā* with a silk thread upon his hand and enjoys [sexual union] will certainly possess stable virility.

On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, having bound [the root] around his waist with a concentrated mind, he should extract the root of the *lāṅgalikā* plant; and during the month of Siṃha, he may likewise take roots such as those of the *makara*.
Now, regarding the strength-increasing [rite]:
one should uproot the root of *ārdraka* under the asterism Kṛttikā.
Having cast it into the mouth and even having drunk liquor, when he goes into the forest, [his strength increases].
One who possesses great strength and great heroism, like an elephant, slays [the enemy] without a doubt.
Now, the method for retaining what has been heard:
having brought the root of the *dhātrī* plant, one should grind it together with sesame seeds.
By consuming it every morning for one month, a man shall become a possessor of the Vedas.
Now, regarding the practice of wielding weapons: having brought the root of the *māla* plant and bound it upon his hand, he went into the forest;
from then on, weapons never fell upon his body.
(p. 35) Now follows the description of the throbbing of the limbs.
Hereafter, I shall fully explain the results arising from the throbbing of the limbs.
Having known which, a person may understand the results of both the auspicious and the inauspicious.
Trembling of the head indicates sovereignty; the forehead is the cause of disease;
there is gain in the right eye, and quarrel in the left eye.
And [he related] the news of the grief of both, as well as my own death by drowning in the waves.
If there is throbbing at the upper lip, there will be a quarrel; at the lower lip, a meal of sweets.
By the throbbing at the root of the teeth, one will certainly eat meat.
By means of vibration, one may hear the song of the fruits even in the ears;
in the throat, the yoga consisting of Māra may at times become like life itself.
Gain of wealth on the right arm; gain of a woman on the left arm.
Prosperity and increase on the right side of the back; and the wife of another on the left.
If both [lines] are at the navel, there will be an increase of prosperity; if they are at the navel, death will occur.
On the right hip, there is the gain of clothing; on the left, the meeting with a friend. On both hips, there is a festival; and on the penis, a young woman.
The attainment of a land [is indicated] by a mark on the right cheek; intelligence by one on the left; and wealth by marks on both.
Travel to a foreign land occurs when it is on the private parts; fear of the king when on the right foot;
travel when on the left foot; and service to the king when it is on both feet.
In this way, one should cause the *spanda* to be inscribed, and one shall obtain the fruits of both auspicious and inauspicious [actions].
Thus ends the *Gaurīkāñcalikātantra* from the *Śrīharagaurīsaṃvāda*.
